en: Evan Cole had been dead eleven years.
The only person Nora could interview was his sister.
Rebecca Cole lived in an old apartment building on the north side. A faded blue wind chime hung beside the door.
She did not invite Nora inside.
"I'm not here to retry his case."
Rebecca's hand stopped on the door.
The name meant nothing to her.
Nora showed her a photograph of Lena.
"Knew her well enough to ruin his life."
"Why did he buy gasoline that night?"
Nora rested one hand against the outside of the frame, not blocking it.
"Police said that gasoline was used to set the fire. But they never found the container."
"Was there another reason he needed gasoline?"
Rebecca was silent for a long time.
The living room was crowded with plants.
She pulled a plastic folder from the bottom shelf of a bookcase.
"I didn't keep this because I thought someday I'd overturn his conviction."
"Because if I threw everything away, it would be like the only Evan left was the man in the judgment."
"He was helping me fix my garage door," Rebecca said. "I had an old gas generator that wouldn't start. He said he'd come back the next day and work on it."
Martin checked the evidence report the next day.
There had been gasoline in the generator tank.
But nothing could establish that it came from the 4.6 litres Evan bought that night.
"So it doesn't rule out arson," Martin said.
"A court doesn't require absolute proof of every detail."
"No. But why did 'bought gasoline' turn into 'preparation for the offence'?"
Nora opened the prosecution's closing argument.
Evan purchased accelerant less than ninety minutes before the fire.
"He bought gasoline. By closing argument, it had become accelerant."
"The fact didn't change. The relationship changed."
The fire investigation confirmed petroleum-based accelerant residue in the west section of the warehouse. The samples were badly contaminated and could not be tied to a specific commercial source.
More importantly, investigators never recovered the portable red plastic gasoline container Evan had purchased.
"They searched his apartment, his car, Rebecca's place," Nora said. "Where's the can?"
"If he used it to start the fire, why wasn't it there?"
"Then come back and call the fire department?"
"Whatever Evan does, the original story can absorb it."
"If a theory can explain every possible outcome, it may also be impossible to disprove."
Martin was about to answer when his phone rang.
He answered and said yes three times.
When he hung up, his expression had changed completely.
"Elise found an evidence-transfer sheet that was never digitized."
zh: 诺拉只能去见他的妹妹。
Rebecca Cole住在城北一栋老公寓里，门口挂着一块褪色的蓝色风铃。
这个名字显然对她没有意义。
“他为什么十九号晚上买汽油？”
诺拉把手按在门框外侧，没有挡门。
“警方说那桶汽油用于纵火，但桶从没找到。”
“他买汽油是不是还有别的用途？”
Rebecca沉默很久，终于把门打开。
她从书柜下层抽出一只塑料文件夹。
“这些年我留着，不是因为我觉得哪天能翻案。”
“因为如果全扔了，就像他真的只剩下判决书里那个人。”
“我哥哥那时候在帮我修车库门。”Rebecca说，“旧汽油发电机启动不了，他说第二天来弄。”
发电机油箱内确实有汽油。
但没有办法证明是Evan当晚买的那一桶。
“法庭不是靠绝对证明每一个细节。”
“可问题是，这桶汽油为什么从‘可疑行为’变成了‘作案准备’？”
诺拉翻到当年控方结案陈词。
Evan purchased accelerant less than ninety minutes before the fire.
“他买的是汽油。到结案陈词里，它变成了accelerant——助燃剂。”
火灾调查报告显示，仓库西侧确实存在石油类加速剂残留。但样本受污染严重，无法确定具体商品来源。更重要的是，现场没有发现Evan购买的便携式红色塑料油桶。
“当年警察搜过他的住处、车、Rebecca家。”诺拉说，“桶呢？”
“如果他拿去纵火，为什么现场没有？”
“不管Evan做什么，都可以被原来的故事解释。”
“一个故事如果能解释所有结果，也可能意味着它根本无法被反驳。”
接通后，他只说了三次“是”。
挂断时，表情已经完全变了。
“伊莉丝找到了一份没有数字化的证物转移单。”
